# PyPath — v0.4.0 (level projects, glossary, cheat sheets, certificate)

A beginner-focused Python learning app for Android. Native Kotlin + Jetpack Compose (Material 3).

Onboarding → dashboard → levels → sub-levels → lesson → MCQs → completion, with progress saved on the device, plus a **Practical** tab where learners write and run real Python on the phone. Seven levels (Basics → Final project), a guided Level 7 project, a badge celebration for every level and short sound effects. No ads, subscriptions or payments.

## Generated files (run on GitHub, no PC needed)

`content/build_course.py` (course JSON) and `content/build_sounds.py` (WAV sound effects) are the sources of truth.
After changing either, run **Actions → Generate course and sounds**. It validates the course, writes
`app/src/main/assets/course/**` and `app/src/main/res/raw/*.wav`, and commits them. Then run **Build APK**.
The app also builds without the WAV files (it is just silent).

## Build

Requirements: JDK 17 and the Android SDK (platform 35).

```bash
./gradlew assembleDebug            # app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk
./gradlew assembleRelease          # minified; signed with the debug key for testing only
./gradlew testDebugUnitTest        # progression, content and MCQ engine tests
./gradlew recordPaparazziDebug     # renders screen snapshots to app/src/test/snapshots
./gradlew connectedDebugAndroidTest # on a device/emulator: real Python execution + Practical UI tests
```

Min SDK 26 (Android 8.0), target SDK 35.

## Architecture

```
app/src/main/
├─ assets/course/course.json        ← course index; levels/l1.json … l7.json hold the content (generated by content/build_course.py)
├─ res/raw/*.wav                    ← sound effects (generated by content/build_sounds.py)
└─ java/com/pypath/app/
   ├─ PyPathApp.kt                  AppContainer (manual DI: swap repositories here)
   ├─ MainActivity.kt               splash (held until progress loads) + edge-to-edge
   ├─ audio/SoundManager.kt         SoundPool effects (Learn side only, never the Practical tab)
   ├─ data/
   │  ├─ model/CourseModels.kt      Course → Level → SubLevel → steps, Lesson pages/blocks, Quiz/Question
   │  ├─ content/CourseRepository   interface + asset JSON implementation + CourseParser
   │  └─ progress/                  UserProgress model + DataStore-backed ProgressRepository
   ├─ domain/Progression.kt         CourseSnapshot: the only place that decides lock/unlock/current
   └─ ui/
      ├─ theme/                     colours (light/dark), Plus Jakarta Sans + JetBrains Mono, shapes
      ├─ components/                buttons, cards, pills, progress bar/ring, status node, CodeBlock, Python highlighter
      ├─ mcq/                       reusable MCQ engine (McqSession) + question/option/feedback UI
      ├─ navigation/NavGraph.kt     all routes
      ├─ badges/                    Canvas badge art + full-screen level celebrations
      └─ screens/                   onboarding, dashboard, level, sublevel, lesson, quiz, completion, project
```

### Key rules
- Content is **data**, not code. Adding a level or sub-level = edit `content/build_course.py`, run it, rebuild. No Kotlin changes.
- A sub-level is complete only when **every step in `steps`** is done. Today that's `learn` + `quiz`. The quiz step counts only when the learner reaches the `passPercent` (default 60%).
- Sub-levels unlock in order across the whole course. Levels with `"available": false` show as "Coming soon".
- Progress is stored as versioned JSON in DataStore: onboarding flag, current sub-level, completed steps, completion time, last/best MCQ score, attempts, project resume state and earned badges (schema 2; schema-1 data is migrated and finished levels get their badge silently).
- Settings (Sound effects on/off) live in a separate DataStore, so Reset progress keeps them.

## v0.4.0 extras (all offline)

- **Level projects**: one optional guided project per level (Levels 1–6), built stage by stage like the Expense Tracker. Each one unlocks when its level is finished and never blocks progress, badges or "Continue Learning". They live in `Level.projects` (ids `l1p1` … `l6p1`, codes `1.P` … `6.P`).
  - 1.P Party Bill Splitter, 2.P Movie Ticket Pricer, 3.P Number Guessing Game, 4.P Python Quiz Game, 5.P To-Do List, 6.P Mini Text Adventure.
- **Glossary**: `assets/course/glossary.json`, searchable, filter by level, each term links to the lesson that teaches it.
- **Cheat sheets**: `Level.cheatSheet`, a one-page summary per level that unlocks when the level is finished. "Copy as text" copies it.
- **Certificate**: unlocks after Level 7. It's drawn on the phone (`CertificateRenderer`, android.graphics) with the learner's name, date, stats, badges and a certificate ID. You can share it through Android's share sheet (via a `FileProvider` on `cache/certificates`) or save it to Pictures/PyPath on Android 10+. No permissions are added.
- Source for all of this: `content/course_extras.py`. `build_course.py` imports it, runs every project and snippet with real Python and checks the outputs.

## Where future features plug in

| Feature | Hook |
|---|---|
| Level-final projects / assessments | `Level.finalAssessment`; gate in `CourseSnapshot`; `McqSession` can be reused for assessments |
| Recall system | `SubLevelProgress.completedAt` / quiz history; `McqSession` takes any question list |
| XP, badges, animations | derive from `UserProgress`; add fields with defaults (schema stays backward compatible) |
| Remote content / cloud sync | new `CourseRepository` / `ProgressRepository` implementation in `AppContainer` |
| Premium, rewarded ads | not implemented; would sit in a separate module behind `AppContainer` |

Settings menu (⋮ on the dashboard) has **Sound effects** and **Reset progress** (clears progress and badges).

## Practical tab (real Python)

The bottom navigation has two tabs: **Learn** (the existing dashboard) and **Practical**.

- **Runtime**: [Chaquopy](https://chaquo.com/chaquopy/) 17 (open source, MIT) bundles CPython **3.11** in the APK, for `arm64-v8a`, `armeabi-v7a`, `x86_64` and `x86`. Everything runs on the device - no server, no AI, no network. (3.11 is the newest Chaquopy Python that still ships 32-bit ABIs.)
- **Process isolation**: learner code runs in `PythonRunnerService` in its own process (`:python`). The UI process never runs Python, so `while True: pass` cannot freeze the app. **Stop** and the **10 s execution limit** (time spent waiting for `input()` is not counted) kill that process; a fresh interpreter starts automatically. Crashes or out-of-memory errors only take down that process.
- **I/O**: `app/src/main/python/pypath_runner.py` executes the code with `exec()` in a fresh `__main__` namespace. stdout/stderr and `input()` requests go to the service over OS pipes and are streamed to the console. `input()` shows an input field inside the console; the answer is written back to the waiting program.
- **Errors**: real CPython tracebacks (runner frames removed) are shown in the console; the error card shows the exception and a "Go to line N" shortcut parsed from the traceback.
- **Network lock (kernel)**: the app holds `INTERNET` for cloud backup (main process only). Before any learner code runs, `pypath_netlock.py` installs a seccomp-bpf filter in the `:python` process (all threads, inherited by new threads/children, cannot be removed): `socket()` is refused for every domain except AF_NETLINK and AF_UNIX datagram (logging), so IPv4/IPv6 TCP/UDP, raw sockets and the DNS proxy are unreachable; `ptrace`, `process_vm_*` and `io_uring_*` are refused. `warm_up` fails and `run` refuses to execute code if the lock or its self-test fails.
- **Sandbox (best effort)**: A permanent PEP 578 audit hook blocks sockets, subprocess/exec/fork/kill, ctypes, thread creation and any file access outside a per-run scratch directory (wiped after each run) and the read-only standard library - learner code cannot read app data such as saved progress. The Java bridge modules are hidden and `java`, `android`, `socket`, `subprocess`, `ctypes`, `urllib`, `http`, ... cannot be imported. A Python-level sandbox is not a hard security boundary against a determined attacker; the OS-level protections (separate process, kernel network lock, the Supabase session kept encrypted in the main process only) are the real boundary.
- **No permanent storage**: task code is kept in memory (`PracticalViewModel`) for the session only. It is never written to disk, uploaded or synced. (Only Premium "My programs" are saved, on the phone; see below.)
- **Editor**: `CodeEditor` is a real `BasicTextField` (cursor, selection, copy/paste, hardware keyboards) with syntax highlighting, line numbers, auto-indent after `:`, Tab/Shift+Tab, and a shortcut key bar (Tab, unindent, brackets, quotes, operators).
- **Tasks**: `app/src/main/assets/practical/tasks.json`. Each task names `afterSubLevel` - the sub-level that teaches its last required concept - and unlocks only when that sub-level is completed. Tasks for unreleased levels (loops, lists) show "Coming soon". The Free playground is always open. The sub-level screen links its Practice step to its task.

Files: `practical/` (runner service, client, protocol, task catalog), `ui/screens/practical/` (screen, editor, view model), `ui/navigation/BottomTabs.kt`, `src/main/python/pypath_runner.py`, `src/androidTest/` (on-device tests).

## Google Sign-In

Google sign-in using Android **Credential Manager** (`androidx.credentials` + `googleid`). Guests can
take the first lesson; everything after it needs an account (see **Accounts, guest limit and Privacy
Policy** below).

- **Flow**: after onboarding (and once for existing learners after updating) a sign-in screen offers
  **Sign in with Google** (create an account), **Login with Google** (existing account only) and
  **Continue without sign in** (guest). Sign in or sign out any time from the dashboard menu.
- **What is stored**: the Google account id, email, display name and given name (`pypath_account`), and
  the Supabase session (`pypath_cloud_session`), encrypted with an AES-256-GCM key kept in the Android
  Keystore. The Google ID token is used once and never stored. "Reset progress" does not sign out,
  and signing out does not touch progress or settings on the phone.
- **Supabase sign-in**: the Google ID token is exchanged for a Supabase session
  (`POST /auth/v1/token?grant_type=id_token`, provider `google`). A fresh nonce per attempt: Google
  receives its SHA-256, Supabase the raw value. The learner counts as signed in only if Supabase
  accepts the token. Sign out ends the Supabase session (`/auth/v1/logout`) and clears it from the phone.
  Accounts saved by older versions (before cloud sign-in) are shown as signed out once, with data kept.
- **Uses of the account**: the dashboard greets the learner by first name, and an empty certificate
  name is pre-filled with the Google name (a name the learner typed is never overwritten).
  The avatar shows initials instead of downloading the profile photo.

## Cloud backup (Supabase)

Signed-in learners get a private backup in `public.user_cloud_state` (one row per user, protected by
the project's Row Level Security). Guests never sync. Code: `app/src/main/java/com/pypath/app/cloud/`.

- **What is synced**: learning progress (`progress`), question history / XP per day / streaks
  (`activity`), saved programs (`programs`) and preferences that follow the learner (`settings`: sound,
  certificate name, daily goal, learning minutes). The study reminder (needs this phone's notification
  permission) and the Premium test switch are not synced. Premium is never granted from cloud data.
- **Safe merge, never a blind overwrite**: each sync downloads the row, merges it with the phone's data
  (`CloudMerge`: completed steps, badges, tasks and active days are unions; counters take the larger
  value; the newer program text wins; deleted programs are remembered so they don't come back; each
  setting keeps its newest change), then writes back with an optimistic `revision` check. If another
  phone wrote first, it downloads, merges and retries. "Reset progress" is synced too (newest reset wins).
- **When**: after sign-in, on app start, a few seconds after local changes, and when the app goes to the
  background. Offline changes stay on the phone and are sent later (automatic retry).
- **Several accounts on one phone**: data is never uploaded to a different account. If another account
  signs in, the previous account's local data is kept aside on the phone and merged back the next time
  that account signs in.
- **Keys**: only the Supabase URL and publishable key are in the app (`cloud/SupabaseConfig.kt`); no
  service-role key, database password or OAuth client secret.

### One-time setup (Google Cloud Console)

1. Run **Build APK** once and copy the **package name** (`com.pypath.app`) and **Signing certificate
   SHA-1** from the run Summary (or `apk-info.txt`). Keep using the same signing key
   (`DEBUG_KEYSTORE_BASE64`), otherwise the SHA-1 changes and sign-in stops working.
2. [Google Cloud Console](https://console.cloud.google.com/) > APIs & Services > **OAuth consent screen**:
   set it up (External; add your Gmail as a test user while the app is in Testing).
3. Credentials > Create credentials > **OAuth client ID** > type **Android**: package `com.pypath.app`,
   the SHA-1 from step 1.
4. Credentials > Create credentials > **OAuth client ID** > type **Web application**. Copy its **Client ID**.
5. Paste that Web client ID into `app/src/main/res/values/google_auth.xml`
   (`google_web_client_id`) and run **Build APK** again.

Until step 5 is done the app works exactly as before; the Google button just says sign-in is not set
up yet. The error "Developer console is not set up correctly" means the package name / SHA-1 of the
Android client does not match the installed APK, or the Web client ID is wrong.

Files: `auth/GoogleSignIn.kt` (Credential Manager flow + pure helpers), `data/auth/AuthRepository.kt`
(saved account), `ui/screens/signin/SignInScreen.kt` (screen, Google button, avatar),
`ui/components/AccountDialog.kt`, `res/values/google_auth.xml`, `test/.../GoogleAuthTest.kt`.

## Accounts, guest limit and Privacy Policy

### Three ways in
- **Sign in with Google** (primary) creates a PyPath account, or opens it if this Google account
  already has one (never a duplicate: Supabase Auth links one user per Google identity).
- **Login with Google** (secondary) opens an existing account only. The app sends the Google ID token
  to the `google-account-check` Edge Function, which verifies it with Google's public keys and asks the
  database (service role, server side) whether a Supabase Auth user with that Google identity exists.
  If not, nothing is created and the app shows **Account not found.** / **Don't have an account?** with a
  **Sign in with Google** button that continues sign-up with the same Google account (it asks Google
  again if the token is too old). If the Edge Function is not deployed, Login fails closed with a
  message and Sign in with Google still works.
- **Continue without sign in**: guest mode (local only, never synced).

Cancelled pickers, no network and other failures show a message and leave the learner on the screen.
Account existence is never derived from the `user_cloud_state` row. The check endpoint needs a valid
Google ID token for this app (no token = no answer) and is rate limited (30 / IP and 10 / Google
account per 10 minutes, hashed keys only). No privileged key is in the APK.

### Guest limit
Guests get only the first lesson (`Progression.guestLessonId`), opened automatically. After it the
**You've completed your first lesson!** screen offers **Sign in with Google to Continue** and **Login
with Google to Continue**. Later lessons, sub-levels, quizzes, projects, level completions, the
certificate and Premium screens are locked in `Progression` (`guestLimited`) and every navigation route
is guarded in `NavGraph` (`guard()`), so cards, shortcuts, back navigation, restarts or edited local
progress cannot open them.

### Guest progress and account switching (isolation)
The phone's live stores hold exactly one profile at a time: `SyncMeta.owner` = an account id, or
`null` = guest (`cloud/CloudSync.kt`). A null owner is never treated as permission to merge.
- When an account becomes active (Sign in, Login, app start with a stored session, first sync), the
  guest progress is set aside in the guest slot (`files/cloud/unsynced-guest-local.json`), never
  uploaded, and the account starts from its own cloud copy. Existing cloud progress is never
  overwritten by guest data.
- Signing out (or an expired session) keeps the account's unsynced changes aside for that account only
  and puts the guest progress back. The next person on the phone (guest or another account) never sees
  or receives the previous account's data; a kept-aside copy reaches only its own account.
- **Add guest progress to this account** (account > Privacy & account) is the only way guest progress
  reaches an account: an explicit, explained action, available only with valid consent, after the
  server accepted the session (destination check). Lessons, quiz results, XP history and saved
  programs are merged in; nothing in the account is removed and account settings stay. The guest copy
  stays on the phone. Nothing is deleted to "solve" isolation.
- Not per account (device-local, never uploaded): study reminders and the Premium Phase 2 local
  stores (Quiz Arena results, battle records, study store) and the Premium test switch.

### Audience (12+), mandatory Privacy Policy and consent withdrawal
PyPath is a Python-learning app designed for learners aged **12 and up**. There is no 18+ restriction:
teenagers can use guest mode and can create an account. The sign-in screen says that PyPath is designed
for ages 12+ and asks under-18s to check with a parent or guardian before creating an account.

After Sign in **or** Login, and before the dashboard, a scrollable policy screen
(`ui/screens/privacy/PrivacyConsentScreen.kt`, text in `app/src/main/assets/legal/privacy_policy.txt`,
web copy in `docs/privacy-policy.md`) requires two ticks: **I have read and agree to the Privacy
Policy.** and **I am 18 or older, or I am 12 to 17 and my parent or guardian has read this Privacy
Policy and agrees to me using a PyPath account.** **Agree and Continue** is enabled only when both are
ticked (scrolling is not consent). This age statement is **self-declared**: PyPath does not check age
and does **not** verify a parent's or guardian's identity or consent, and neither the app nor the policy
claims it does. No date of birth or parent details are collected. **I'm under 12** explains that PyPath
is designed for ages 12+ and offers deleting the account at once or signing out; guest mode stays
available. If the app is closed, the screen comes back on the next launch.
Consent is an append-only event log in `public.privacy_consents` (policy version, server timestamp,
status `agreed`/`withdrawn`, `age_confirmed`; RLS: own rows only, insert only). The **newest** row
decides; every sync re-checks it on the server, so a withdrawal (also from another phone) stops syncing.
Policy version is now `2026-11-13.2` (material change: everyone agrees again).

**Withdraw consent** (account > Privacy & account): explained in a dialog; records a `withdrawn` row on
the server first (if that fails, nothing changes and an error is shown), then stops syncing (no final
upload) and signs out to guest mode. The account and cloud backup stay until the learner deletes the
account; the screen points to **Delete my account** for erasure.

**Delete my account** (account > Privacy & account): explains that deletion is permanent and requires
typing `DELETE`. The `delete-account` Edge Function verifies the caller's own Supabase token (the user id
always comes from that token, never from the request, so nobody can delete another account), then
calls `public.pypath_delete_account_data(user_id)` (migration `20261115000000`, executable only by the
service role) which deletes that user's `user_cloud_state` row, all `privacy_consents` rows and any
pending sign-up note, and finally deletes the Supabase Auth user. Every step is safe to retry. The app
shows success only after `{"deleted":true}`; a missing function (404), a gateway rejection (Verify JWT
left on), an expired session, a server failure at any stage or a network error is shown as "NOT
deleted" / "could not confirm". After success the session and the account's copy on the phone are
removed and the app returns to the welcome / sign-in screen (guest progress on the phone is kept).
Retention note: consent records are deleted together with the account, as the app's policy says. If
your lawyer decides you must keep proof of consent for a period, change this deliberately (and the
policy text) rather than leaving orphaned rows.

Account-deletion fixes (Nov 2026), found by code audit (the live project could not be inspected):
1. The function used only the legacy `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`. Projects that use the new API keys
   (or disable legacy keys) do not have a working value there; the functions now use the automatically
   provided `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEYS` / `SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEYS` and fall back to the legacy keys.
2. There was no `supabase/config.toml`, so a Dashboard/CLI deploy kept "Verify JWT" ON; with the new
   JWT signing keys the gateway then rejects every user token with 401 before the function runs, and
   the app misreported that as "sign-in expired". `config.toml` now sets `verify_jwt = false` for both
   functions and the app reports a gateway 401 as a server configuration problem.
3. Data cleanup relied on `ON DELETE CASCADE` alone (a `privacy_consents` table created before the
   migration may lack it) and left sign-up notes behind; it is now explicit (see above).
4. After deletion the app went to the guest dashboard; it now returns to the welcome / sign-in screen.

### Returning-user login (Nov 2026)
Root cause of "Login repeats the introduction": right after sign-in the account's profile on the phone
is empty and the cloud copy was merged only by a later background sync, but the app chose the next
screen immediately from that empty profile (`onboardingCompleted = false`), so it showed onboarding
again (and the setup questions could overwrite the account's daily goal). A fresh install also showed
the introduction before the sign-in screen.
Now: the app opens on the welcome / sign-in screen; after the server-verified sign-in (and the Privacy
Policy, if not yet agreed for the current version) it shows "Restoring your progress…", downloads and
merges the account's cloud copy (normal merge rules: never overwritten with empty local data), and then
decides from the account's data (`domain/AuthFlow.kt`): onboarding done -> straight to the dashboard;
new account (server check said "created") -> introduction and setup questions once. If the cloud copy
cannot be loaded (offline) for an existing account, the learner still goes to the dashboard with a
notice and the data arrives with the next sync. Login with Google for an unknown account shows
"Account not found. Please use Sign in with Google to create an account." and creates nothing.

### Practical Check: completion saving (Nov 2026)
Found while auditing intermittent "correct code but not marked completed": (a) a cloud-sync update of
saved programs could stop a running Check and clear its results even on the Tasks view; (b) the task
screen could switch task (cancelling the Check) when the course snapshot briefly changed; (c) the
completion was written fire-and-forget on the screen's scope with errors swallowed, so a failed or
cancelled write (e.g. app closed right after passing) was lost silently. Now syncs never touch a task
Check, the task is never switched while a Check runs, and `practical/CompletionSaver.kt` stores the
completion on the app scope (not cancelled with the screen), retries, shows "Saving…" and, on failure,
"Try saving again". Empty code shows a message; repeated taps are ignored while a Check runs. The
Python runner, test cases and expected-output checks are unchanged.

Not a legal guarantee: this implementation has not been reviewed by a lawyer and does not by itself
make PyPath compliant with Google Play policies or India's DPDP Act / Rules. Under India's DPDP Act
anyone under 18 is a child, and processing a child's data needs verifiable parental consent (Section 9,
DPDP Rules Rule 10). PyPath has **no** verifiable parental consent mechanism yet (only the learner's
self-declaration), so a legal review of the 12–17 account flow is required before release. The Google
Play content rating is **not** set by this code: complete the official IARC content-rating
questionnaire and the Target audience and content section in Play Console yourself, and check which
of Google Play's current policies for apps with child or teen audiences apply to the age groups you
select there.

**Before release** replace every `[... to be filled in by the app owner]` placeholder in both policy
files (operator name, contact email, postal address, grievance officer, hosting region).

**New policy version**: edit the text, set `PrivacyPolicy.VERSION`; for material changes also set
`RENEWAL_REQUIRED_SINCE` to the same value so every signed-in learner must agree again.

### Google Web client ID (token audience)
The Android app requests Google ID tokens for the **Web** OAuth client ID in
`app/src/main/res/values/google_auth.xml` (`google_web_client_id`). That file is the source of truth:

`366083223668-ghnav157lrq95l3cucvsejkd8l3qv4h3.apps.googleusercontent.com`

Note the lowercase letter `l` (not the digit `1`) in `...q95l3...` and `...kd8l3...`. Supabase and the
Edge Function must use **exactly** this value, otherwise every token is rejected as a wrong audience:
- Supabase Dashboard > Authentication > Sign In / Providers > Google > **Client IDs**: this Web client ID
  (and its client secret in the secret field, entered only in the Dashboard; never in the app or repo).
- Edge Function secret `GOOGLE_WEB_CLIENT_ID` = the same value (copy it from `google_auth.xml`, do not
  retype it). A malformed value makes `google-account-check` answer 500 `server_not_configured`.
- Manual check: Google Cloud Console > APIs & Services > Credentials > OAuth 2.0 Client IDs > the
  **Web application** client: its ID must equal the value above. The Android OAuth client (package
  `com.pypath.app` + SHA-1) is unchanged and is not used as the audience.

### Supabase setup (one time, Dashboard only, free tier)
1. **SQL Editor** > New query > paste and run, in this order (each once; all are safe to re-run, none
   drops tables or touches `user_cloud_state`'s structure or policies):
   - REQUIRED `supabase/migrations/20261113000000_pypath_privacy_consent_and_account_check.sql`
     (skip if already applied),
   - REQUIRED `supabase/migrations/20261114000000_pypath_consent_withdrawal_and_age.sql`
     (withdrawal events, `age_confirmed` = self-declared age statement),
   - REQUIRED `supabase/migrations/20261115000000_pypath_account_deletion.sql`
     (NEW: `pypath_delete_account_data`, used by `delete-account`; without it the function falls back
     to deleting the two tables through the REST API),
   - OPTIONAL hardening `supabase/migrations/20261113000100_pypath_optional_signup_guard_hook.sql`.
2. **Edge Functions** — redeploy BOTH (the code changed), JWT verification OFF for both (they verify
   the caller themselves; `supabase/config.toml` sets this for CLI deploys):
   - `supabase functions deploy google-account-check --no-verify-jwt` (REQUIRED for Login with Google)
   - `supabase functions deploy delete-account --no-verify-jwt` (REQUIRED for Delete my account)
   Without the CLI: Dashboard > Edge Functions > the function > Code > replace `index.ts` with the file
   from this repo > Deploy (or Deploy a new function > Via Editor with the exact name if it does not
   exist yet), then open its **Details/Settings** and make sure **Verify JWT** is OFF.
   Then check Edge Functions > `delete-account` > Logs while deleting a test account.
3. **Edge Function secrets** (Dashboard > Edge Functions > Secrets): `GOOGLE_WEB_CLIENT_ID` = the Web
   client ID above; optional `RATE_LIMIT_SALT` = any long random string. `SUPABASE_URL`,
   `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEYS` / `SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEYS` (new keys) and the legacy
   `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` / `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` are provided by Supabase automatically; do not add
   them yourself and never put them in the app.
4. Optional: Authentication > Hooks > **Before User Created** > Postgres > `public.pypath_before_user_created`
   (only after steps 1–3 and the new app are live).
5. If other tables of your project reference `auth.users` without `ON DELETE CASCADE`, deleting a user
   fails at the `auth_user` stage (the app then shows that the account was not fully deleted); check
   Database > Tables for such foreign keys and add them to `pypath_delete_account_data` if they hold
   PyPath data.

Local checks: `supabase/functions/*/index_test.ts`
(`PYPATH_FUNCTION_TEST=1 deno test --allow-env --allow-read ...`) and `supabase/tests/*.sql` (plain
PostgreSQL with stubbed Supabase roles; not proof of compatibility with the real Supabase project).

## Premium Phase 1 (Advanced IDE + Image Center)

Free users keep every existing feature exactly as before. Premium adds, on top:

- **Advanced Python IDE** (Practical tab → *My programs*): multiple independent programs, create / rename / edit / delete (with confirmation), folders, a built-in snippets library (26 snippets, inserted at the cursor with matching indentation), autosave (0.7 s after typing stops and whenever the app goes to the background) and restore after restarting the app. It reuses the existing `CodeEditor`, `EditorKeyBar`, Chaquopy runner and console. All programs are stored once in `files/programs/programs.json` (no database, no cloud); an unreadable file is kept as `programs.json.bak`.
- **Image Center** (Certificate → *Image Center*): exactly two PyPath images drawn on the phone (`ImageCenterRenderer`, no image assets): a 1080×2340 JPEG wallpaper and a 1080×1350 PNG Python quick reference. *Download* saves them to Pictures/PyPath through the certificate's MediaStore pipeline (`CertificateExport.saveImageToGallery`); Android 8–9 use a legacy path with `WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE` (declared with `maxSdkVersion="28"`).

**Access** (`premium/PremiumAccess.kt`): screens check one `PremiumFeature` via `Entitlements.has(...)`. In this phase access comes from `LocalDevPremiumRepository`, a local developer/testing switch (dashboard ⋮ → *Premium* → *Premium test mode*, own DataStore file `pypath_premium`). **It is not a purchase and not secure payment verification.** A backend-verified repository can replace it in `AppContainer` later without changing any screen.
